item.title: G7 ministers meet to discuss Ukraine peace talks and US-Iran tensions
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: G7 ministers meet as Europe seeks greater say in Ukraine peace talks
G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris to discuss Europe's role in US-led efforts to end Russia's war in Ukraine and to urge Washington against resuming military action against Iran. The meeting coincides with US-mediated talks between Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot emphasized European participation in the Abu Dhabi talks, stressing that any settlement must not compromise Ukraine's sovereignty. US President Donald Trump suggested a potential deal could alter Ukraine's borders, claiming it would involve all of Europe. European leaders demand inclusion in peace talks and security guarantees for Ukraine. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Trump's envoy Jared Kushner highlighted progress on a broader European security framework. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy expressed skepticism about new security frameworks preceding peace efforts. The G7 also addresses US-Iran tensions, with Trump considering military strikes on suspected Iranian nuclear sites. European governments favor diplomatic solutions over military action, focusing on restoring shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump claimed Iranian officials remain open to negotiations. The Paris meeting marks the end of France's G7 presidency, with the US set to take over in 2027.

item.title: Solana Beach council approves marine safety center expansion plans
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Solana Beach council receives marine safety update
Solana Beach Marine Safety Capt. Greg Uruburu provided an update on El Nino preparedness and seasonal safety operations at the city council meeting. He noted the beach profile and sand levels are favorable for El Nino season, with training focused on swift water rescue and high surf response. Summer statistics show 513 total rescues, up from previous years, but 17,583 safety contacts, a drop of about 20,000 from prior years, attributed to high surf conditions. Uruburu explained the shift in operational focus due to increased surf risks. The city also discussed plans for a new Marine Safety Center, nearly tripling the current facility size. A Coastal Development Permit was submitted in August, with a hearing expected in early 2027. City engineer Austin Frisby outlined a timeline for design finalization in 2027, followed by construction starting in 2028. The project has $1.2 million for design and $4 million for construction, with final costs dependent on Coastal Commission approval.

item.title: NASA seeks astronauts for lunar missions with expanded STEM requirements
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Science Original headline: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
NASA is seeking astronauts to live and work on the Moon. The agency announced a new recruitment process for candidates interested in joining its astronaut corps. Selected astronauts will participate in missions requiring technical expertise, teamwork, and courage, according to NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. Requirements include a master's degree in STEM, now expanded to include nursing, three years of professional experience, or alternatives like PhDs, doctors, or pilots with extensive flight experience. The selection process remains highly competitive, with only 10 candidates chosen from over 8,000 applicants in the last class. Training will last two years, preparing astronauts for missions like landing near the Moon's South Pole. NASA aims to return humans to the Moon by 2028, relying on private companies like Blue Origin and SpaceX. Applications are open until December 3, with a starting salary of $164,395. NASA spokesperson Anna Schneider confirmed nursing degrees are now recognized as STEM qualifications.

item.title: Solana Beach council approves healthy city resolution
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune
Solana Beach City Council voted unanimously Oct. 28 on a resolution to affirm and strengthen the city’s Healthy City initiatives. The resolution establishes a shared framework to coordinate policies and investments impacting health, quality of life, and sustainability. Priority areas include climate resilience, food access, youth wellness, community safety, and active transportation. The agenda report highlights past efforts like smoking bans, plastic restrictions, public arts investments, and multi-modal transportation upgrades. Projects tied to the initiative include Lomas Santa Fe improvements, Fletcher Cove Park upgrades, EV charging expansion, and a senior transportation pilot. Mayor Lesa Heebner emphasized the resolution aligns with Solana Beach’s reputation as an outdoor city, stating it unifies priorities and programs under a 'health in all policies' approach.

item.title: Train Collision in Egypt Leaves Seven Dead, Over 100 Injured
item.description:
Source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle
A train collision near Giza, Egypt, killed at least seven people and injured over 100, according to authorities. Two trains traveling south from Cairo and Giza collided, derailing and sending carriages down an embankment. Emergency responders searched the wreckage for survivors, while hospitals prepared for a surge of patients with severe injuries. The driver of one train died, confirmed by the ministry. The crash occurred between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations, near the site of Egypt’s deadliest train disaster in February 2002, which killed over 370 people. Officials ordered an investigation into the accident’s cause, with President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi demanding accountability. Emergency crews deployed 52 ambulances and cranes to clear the wreckage. Calls for the transport minister’s resignation emerged, and foreign leaders including Saudi Arabia and Turkey expressed condolences. The public prosecutor warned the death toll could rise, highlighting the tragedy’s severity. The railway authority has not yet announced a timeline for full recovery.

item.title: San Diego Restaurants Introduce Fall Flavors Despite Warm Weather
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: How San Diego restaurants are bringing fall flavors to the table despite warm weather
North Italia in San Diego's Fashion Valley launched a fall seasonal menu on October 14, featuring dishes like Burrata di Stagione with Fuji apples and Calabrian agrodolce sauce, and Seasonal Vegetable Salad with roasted Brussels sprouts and white balsamic vinaigrette. New pasta options include Fusilli al Telefono with DiNapoli tomatoes and Tripoline Alfredo with white vodka cream sauce. Crispy Chicken Piccata, served with arugula and marinated artichoke hearts, was highlighted by food critic Gabe Salazar. Pizza fans can try the Double Pepperoni with mozzarella and Grana Padano, available as a flatbread during happy hour. Seasonal beverages like Meet Me in Capri and Diavolo are also offered. The menu includes weekday happy hour ($10 appetizers, $25 two-course lunch) and a $45 prix fixe dinner. While the fall menu is available through winter, specific end dates are not announced. Some dishes remain on the regular menu. North Italia also operates at One Paseo, with details available on its website.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Thanksgiving mashed potatoes recipe and preparation tips
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Kitchen Shrink: A mash made in heaven – Thanksgiving’s best sidekick
Mashed potatoes are a Thanksgiving staple, appearing at 71 percent of American holiday tables. The dish's preparation involves selecting the right potato variety, with russets for lightness and Yukon Golds for creaminess. Cooking methods include mashing or using a ricer to achieve a silky texture, while avoiding low-starch potatoes like Red Bliss. Ingredients range from butter and cream to dairy-free alternatives, with seasonings like salt, pepper, herbs, and spices adding depth. Variations include adding cheese, herbs, or alcohol like bourbon and rum for flavor. Dietary adaptations include olive oil, plant-based butters, and cauliflower mash. A recipe details peeling, boiling, mashing, and garnishing with rosemary and butter. The dish offers numerous customization options, from savory to creamy, catering to diverse tastes and dietary needs.

item.title: Three Killed in CHP Chase Near Baldwin Park
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Three dead after CHP chases suspected drunk driver near Baldwin Park
Three people died after a car fleeing from California Highway Patrol officers crashed into a concrete wall near Baldwin Park Saturday morning. Authorities suspect the driver, operating a 2011 Toyota Corolla, was intoxicated. Officers attempted to stop the vehicle for unsafe driving on the 10 Freeway but pursued it at high speeds. The driver lost control at the Francisquito Avenue off-ramp and struck the wall around 4 a.m. The driver was pronounced dead at the scene, while two passengers died from injuries at separate hospitals. A fourth victim remains hospitalized with major injuries. Police did not release names of the deceased, though one passenger was identified as a 20-year-old man. The CHP did not immediately comment on additional details about the crash.

item.title: Experienced Skydivers Die in Midair Collision During Training
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Former comic, lead instructor identified as Lake Elsinore skydivers killed in midair collision
Experienced skydivers Georgia Jean, 56, and Levi Pimentel, 29, died after colliding midair and becoming entangled during a training session in Lake Elsinore. Authorities confirmed the pair, from South Dakota and Illinois respectively, fell to the ground following the collision approximately 150 feet above the earth. Their parachutes became entangled, leading to their deaths at a local hospital. The incident occurred during an organized event aimed at setting a state record for the largest women’s upright formation skydive. Both were licensed skydivers with extensive experience—Jean had completed over 1,700 jumps and won a bronze medal at the 2024 U.S. Parachute Assn. National Skydiving Championships. Pimentel, a lead instructor at iFLY Indoor Skydiving, had set a women’s head-down world record in 2022. An investigation is ongoing, with the FAA collecting their parachutes for analysis. The collision occurred during a group jump from a plane, with participants holding hands as part of the formation training.

item.title: Houthis strike Aramco Tower in Riyadh, damage reported
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
Houthis launched air strikes targeting Riyadh's financial district, including the Aramco Tower. A statement from Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed attacks on the city's business zone, though the tower was not named. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry reported minor damage with no casualties, while BBC Verify authenticated footage showing extensive damage, including shattered windows and a struck floor. The Houthis also claimed strikes on Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities, which Saudi air defenses intercepted. The attacks mark renewed escalation in the conflict, which intensified after the Iran war. An informal ceasefire collapsed in July following a Houthi maritime embargo and attacks on Saudi infrastructure. The UN reports over 1,600 deaths and 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed. Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of a blockade and an air strike on Sanaa airport, which Saudi denied.

item.title: Cruise Ship Pianist Rescued After Nine Hours in Pacific
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Cruise ship pianist rescued from sea after nine hours in Pacific Ocean
A cruise ship pianist was rescued after spending nine hours in the Pacific Ocean near Catalina Island. Fishermen Grant Garrett and Sean Norton spotted the Royal Caribbean employee, identified as a pianist on the Ovation of the Seas, treading water around 15-20 miles offshore. The man, not yet publicly named, was taken to a hospital in stable condition. Coast Guard officials confirmed the rescue, noting the individual was recovered by a Good Samaritan. Lifeguards estimate he fell overboard around 02:30, surviving the ordeal aided by unusually warm water temperatures of 76 degrees Fahrenheit. Norton attributed his survival to the El Niño-driven warmth, which is currently the strongest on record. Royal Caribbean stated they are supporting the crew member but declined to provide further details. The incident highlights the risks of falling overboard in the Pacific, where temperatures can significantly impact survival chances.

item.title: San Diego County Heatwave Continues Through Friday
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: San Diego County temperatures expected to stay in 80s through Friday
San Diego County will remain in the 80s through Friday as a heatwave persists, with daily highs reaching 80 or above across the region. The National Weather Service warns of continued El Niño-enhanced high tides and powerful waves, with tides exceeding 7 feet daily through Tuesday, peaking at 7.4 to 7.6 feet on Monday. Northwest waves are expected to reach 4 to 7 feet Tuesday, creating dangerous rip currents. Lifeguards are concerned as sea surface temperatures are 11 degrees above average, drawing more beachgoers. Temperatures on Sunday through 2 p.m. ranged from 80 in San Diego to 90 in Allied Gardens. The coast faces ongoing threats from large waves that damaged Del Mar’s berm over the weekend.

item.title: Mission Beach Faces Another Coastal Flood Advisory
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Mission Beach residents brace for high tides again with another coastal flood advisory in effect in San Diego
Another coastal flood advisory is in effect for San Diego's Mission Beach, following major flooding two weeks ago. Residents are preparing for potential water intrusion despite new sand berms designed to block tides. Kevin Mayo, a local resident, expressed concern as high tides approached his garage, with water nearly reaching his home's first-floor room. 'It got within a couple of inches' during the last king tide, he said, warning of damage to flooring and drywall. The city reinforced the berm, which is now larger and stronger, but Mayo plans to use sandbags as a precaution. Tides are predicted to peak above 7 feet, prompting continued efforts to maintain storm drains and use pumps to manage street flooding. Officials reiterated their commitment to reinforcing the berm and addressing drainage issues to mitigate future risks.

item.title: Pedestrian Fatally Struck by Two Vehicles on East Valley Parkway in Escondido
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Pedestrian fatally struck by 2 vehicles on East Valley Parkway in Escondido
A 60-year-old man was struck by two vehicles on East Valley Parkway in Escondido and later died. Police responded to the scene at 8:30 p.m. Saturday, reporting the pedestrian was hit in westbound lanes. The first driver was present and cooperated with investigators, with no drugs or alcohol involved. A second vehicle, described as a small black sports car with tinted windows, struck the man as he lay on the roadway and failed to stop. The vehicle was last seen driving north on Citrus Avenue. Authorities are seeking witnesses to contact EPD Officer Jake Houchin at 760-839-4904. No other injuries were reported.

item.title: Delhi Air Quality Reaches 'Severe' Levels After Diwali Celebrations
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: India news: Delhi air quality level 'severe' after Diwali
Delhi's air quality reached 'severe' levels after Diwali celebrations, with residents violating a firecracker ban. Air Quality Index (AQI) in parts of the National Capital Region (NCR) exceeded WHO limits by over 50 times, with PM 2.5 levels in central Delhi reaching 879 micrograms per cubic meter—nearly 59 times the recommended limit. Smog reduced visibility, and health risks escalated. The pollution crisis, worsened by winter conditions, crop-residue fires, and vehicle emissions, has plagued Delhi for years. Despite restrictions on conventional firecrackers and winter pollution rules, enforcement failed. Meanwhile, ousted Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina requested a new passport from India to facilitate her return to Bangladesh, where she faces extradition demands. Bangladesh's foreign affairs minister stated she is a 'fugitive criminal' and emphasized the active extradition treaty with India.

item.title: Carruth Cellars Marks 20th Anniversary with Two-Day Event
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Carruth Cellars to celebrate 20 years with two-day anniversary party
Carruth Cellars is hosting a two-day anniversary celebration from Nov. 14-15 at its Solana Beach Tasting Room to mark 20 years in business. Founded in 2006, the urban winery expanded to four locations across San Diego County. Founder Adam Carruth emphasized the community and friendships built over two decades, stating the event is about thanking supporters. The party includes 12 exclusive wine tastings, an unlimited gourmet buffet by Chef Luke Morganstern, live music, and special pricing on reserve wines. Attendees will receive a limited-edition commemorative glass and a raffle entry for prizes. Tickets cost $80 for the public or $64 for members, offering access to all activities. The event is 21+ only, with no children, dogs, or outside food allowed. Regular business at the Solana Beach location will be closed during the event.

item.title: South Korean City Uses U.S. College Model to Counter AI Education Challenges
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: News Original headline: Why a South Korean city is turning to a U.S. college to outsmart AI?
Chuncheon, South Korea, is adopting the 'Great Books' educational model from St. John's College in Maryland to address concerns about AI's role in education. Teachers at Toegye public elementary school use Socratic discussions to explore themes like AI's humanity, with students debating whether AI possesses creativity. The model emphasizes critical thinking over rote memorization, with no lectures, majors, or internet use. South Korea faces declining PISA reading scores and widespread AI chatbot use, with 51% of students relying on AI for studying. Critics, like English professor Lee Yonghwa, argue AI undermines students' ability to reason and judge information. Chuncheon Mayor Yook Dong-han launched a partnership with St. John's College in 2023, now serving 120 college students and 770 younger learners. Students engage with texts like Aristotle, Shakespeare, and Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'Letter from Birmingham Jail,' linking historical ideas to modern issues like South Korea's 2024 martial law debate. Lee notes the program fosters civic engagement, aiming to 'stitch the fabric of our democracy' through collaborative learning.
